theory.overview: Bit manipulation uses bitwise operators to work at the level of individual bits. It's fundamental for low-level programming, compression, cryptography, and certain optimization problems. Key operations include AND (&), OR (|), XOR (^), NOT (~), Left Shift (<<), and Right Shift (>>). Bit manipulation enables compact representations (bit masks), efficient arithmetic (powers of 2), and clever algorithms for subset generation, power of two checks, and finding single numbers.

keyConcepts.name: Basic Bitwise Operators
keyConcepts.description: AND (&): both bits must be 1. OR (|): at least one bit is 1. XOR (^): exactly one bit is 1. NOT (~): flips all bits.

keyConcepts.name: Bit Shifts
keyConcepts.description: Left shift (<<): multiply by 2^n. Right shift (>>): divide by 2^n. Unsigned right shift (>>>): fills with zeros.

keyConcepts.name: Common Tricks
keyConcepts.description: n & (n-1) clears lowest set bit. n & (-n) isolates lowest set bit. n ^ n = 0, n ^ 0 = n.

keyConcepts.name: Bitmask Applications
keyConcepts.description: Represent subsets of n elements as n-bit integers. DP with bitmasks solves exponential problems efficiently for small n.

complexity.countSetBits: O(log n) or O(1) with lookup
